title: Jako
type: Goblin naturalist and earthworker · First Called
dek: A hesitant goblin who finds a voice through shared minds, helps build Pristinia and keeps asking what saving people means when hunger, disease and money divide them.

facts.Early company: First Called · Day 1 of the Final War
facts.Skills: Fungal magic, earth shaping, gathering and cooking
facts.Later record: Selected quest scenes reach the Month of Physisia, Year 1; subsequent fate not established

body:
Jako comes through the Gate cautiously, a small ash-grey goblin with gathering clothes and a cap. They have spent so long quietly collecting herbs and fungus that spoken words sometimes fail them. Their wish to help is real before they can express it fluently. The first company gives that wish people to attach to and a town in which to practice it.

A mind answered by another mind

The gods’ warning of Death frightens Jako. Hearing an answer to thoughts they have not spoken is frightening too, but also makes conversation possible. They wonder whether there will be a home where they can learn to face the threat. Scribonia’s telepathy offers a familiar way to share pictures, words and memories of spores and sunlight.

Jako follows the company and accepts a place on Scribonia’s shoulders when their short legs cannot keep up. In the first fight, they use spores and roots against the undead, stay close to him and try to help even when the trick fails. Fear remains visible in the way they act; it does not keep them out of the company.

Earthwork, mushrooms and friends

At Pristinia’s work gathering, Jako arrives breathless with a plate of cooked mushrooms. Cooking is something they want to learn: home offered little beyond mushrooms roasted over a fire. They are delighted when someone is willing to teach them.

They vote to continue the wall and offer to shape earth. The work looks almost playful as they move and compact the ground, while conversations with Ryvyt and Elenia continue around it. They encourage Nienna, notice when Elenia seems unwell and try to reassure friends about gathering safely near town. Their contribution to a defensible settlement is also a way of becoming less alone.

A reason to leave a creature alone

When companions discuss wild animals, Jako argues against destroying or moving them without need. Scarcity already makes life difficult outside; changing a habitat can kill what the company means to spare. They would leave a beast alone unless it poses a danger.

That outlook has teeth. In the later water investigation, Jako confronts armed thugs with fungal growth, a glowing stare and thunder. Even while permitting retreat, they send one last cloud of spores after an opponent. Compassion for living things has not made them harmless or free of anger.

The people who make room for them

John calls for his sporeous friend when he returns to town, and Jako greets him with affection. John cannot promise that the struggle against Death will never take him away again; he promises to try to return. Jako’s place beside a confident protector gives the early militia story a personal bond.

Later, Dale carries Jako on his back while they watch a difficult negotiation. When Jako loses heart over people suffering for coin, Dale’s music calms them a little. Being cared for does not instantly settle what they think about the people they are trying to save.

Choosing the water over the argument

Jako notices the poor condition of the streets and thinks about hygiene, soap and the source of fresh water. The social encounter leaves them frustrated: they cannot understand why money should make people refuse help or cause so much suffering.

Their response is to leave the stalled conversation and look for the water source through signs of decay and disease around the harbor. The selected account follows that choice, not a completed cure or an answer to every injustice they have seen. Read the first company’s arrival →
